key_insight: As synthetic training budgets grow, expanding tool and database diversity improves tool-use agent generalization more than adding tasks alone.
engineering_relevance: Synthetic-data pipelines should expose controls for environment diversity and complexity to guide efficient scaling of tool-use agent training.
method: Use SynthAPI to control tool, task, and database diversity.
Systematically vary synthetic environment composition and training scale.
Fit a scaling law predicting downstream generalization.
evidence_signal: The study spans 458,752 tasks and 849 trained models across four sizes, with finding-guided training outperforming prior-work data baselines on four evaluation benchmarks.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether the scaling law transfers to real-world tool ecosystems beyond the evaluated benchmarks.
paper_title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
